reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the presenters actively promote BitClub and BeHappy24 as an MLM business, encourage viewers to build teams and downlines, and tie builder status and community payments to recruitment. They also promote investment portfolios and mining as sources of passive or unusually large returns, including claims of 50 to 2000 percent portfolio gains and passive mining income. The webinar is a promotional recruitment presentation rather than a warning, investigation, or neutral market discussion.

opening.argument: The presentation repeatedly presents proposals as provisional rather than certifying a fixed investment product or guaranteed outcome. The speakers describe the plan as still under consideration, say they may change or remove elements, and acknowledge that no strategy has yet been adopted. They also emphasize cooperation and shared responsibility, including that the community does not do everything for participants. That uncertainty is inconsistent with a deceptive guarantee: viewers are being shown an evolving community proposal whose terms and implementation remain subject to discussion.

citations.quote: This is pre-consideration period when you're working with us.
We're not even sure what strategy we will not committed to.
We, as a community, are not doing everything for you, you need to understand.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited MLM and earnings language shows that business opportunities were discussed, but it does not establish that every proposal was a guaranteed solicitation or that participants were promised risk-free returns. The quoted percentages are attributed to friends' portfolios, while the presentation also describes plans as provisional and subject to participant input. Builder benefits and community payments can therefore be read as conditional program features, not proof of deception.

citations.quote: my friends from the same society had just registered from 50 to 2000 plus percents in their portfolio.
This is pre-consideration period when you're working with us.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The provisional wording concerns the community's future strategy, not a warning that the promoted opportunity is unsafe or that its earnings claims are unverified. The same presentation affirmatively describes an MLM direction intended to help people multiply capital, reports extraordinary portfolio gains, and offers builder subsidies. Uncertainty about future design does not neutralize active promotion of recruitment and financial returns.

opening.argument: The material is best understood as a community webinar explaining proposed tools, training, portfolios, and operating procedures. It explicitly describes a collaborative presentation of slides and a shared vision, and later explains that the planned school would address business, finances, relationships, and self-development. The speakers also demonstrate how a system, referrals, multilingual support, and automated information might work. Discussion of possible earnings within that instructional setting does not by itself convert the whole video into a scam solicitation.

citations.quote: we prepared for the presentation today slides, vision
This is about business, finances, family, relationships and self growth.
it will be fully automated.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it a webinar does not make it neutral education. The presentation describes an MLM direction, five-level depth, builder ranks, and payments connected to placing people in teams. Those are not merely technical demonstrations; they explain how participants can expand the business and receive benefits. The instructional format is precisely how the opportunity is presented to prospective partners.

citations.quote: we have the main direction of MLM
When the deepness is five levels, then you can add another company to AdClub.
If someone puts a builder in my team

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The educational framing does not account for the presentation's concrete recruitment architecture. Its training, automation, referral links, builder levels, and community-funded builder payments are operational instructions for growing the program, not detached lessons. The financial claims are also presented as reasons to participate, so describing the event as a webinar does not remove its promotional function.

citations.quote: the referral links of BitClub, LENDING, CONTACTS and so on are already going to be supplied everywhere
if you do ProBuilder, then 50% is paid by the community pays 50% for you

opening.argument: The evidence is also compatible with ordinary community commerce and services: portfolios involving cryptocurrency, real estate, and precious metals; property renovation and renting; training; automated messaging; and partner travel events. Crucially, the supplied material does not show a request for a deposit, a credential or password, or a guaranteed return. It describes participants doing work themselves and says the community is not doing everything for them. Recruitment language and referral tools can occur in ordinary partner programs without proving that the underlying service is fraudulent.

citations.quote: We, as a community, are not doing everything for you, you need to understand.
It has to be paid for. Because free work is not possible without it.
we continue to work with reliable contractors

rebuttal.rebuttal: The absence of a password request or an explicit guarantee is not decisive. The cited material directly links the program to MLM, capital multiplication, mining, portfolio earnings, team placement, and builder subsidies. Those are the relevant mechanisms here; the fact that the presentation also mentions contractors, training, or travel does not make the recruitment-and-return claims ordinary retail commerce.

citations.quote: we have the main direction of MLM and we established it to make the people earn money to multiply their capital
Mining creates passive income
If someone puts a builder in my team

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The slide and service references do not eliminate the central mechanism. The presentation says the MLM direction is intended to multiply capital, describes passive mining income and unusually large portfolio gains, and ties community money to builder status. A requirement that participants perform work themselves is compatible with recruitment-based promotion; it does not show that the opportunity is an ordinary purchase or that the financial claims are reliable.
